draft.title: Circuits in the home
card: Household appliances are mostly wired in parallel. Each one sits on its own branch, connected across the active and neutral wires from the supply.
In a parallel circuit, every branch has the same voltage across it. In Australian homes this is about 230 V, so each appliance gets the full supply voltage.
Each branch carries its own current. If one appliance is switched off or fails, the other branches are not cut off and keep working.
The current in the main supply wire is the sum of the branch currents. Turning on more appliances adds more branches, so the total current rises.
draft.remember: Parallel branches share the same voltage, work independently, and their currents add.

a.q: A kettle and a toaster are plugged into two sockets on the same household circuit. The toaster is switched off. What happens to the kettle?
opts: It keeps working with the same voltage across it
It works, but with a lower voltage across it
It stops, because the circuit is now broken
It works, but with a higher voltage across it
a.why: The kettle is on its own parallel branch, so switching off the toaster does not break its path. The voltage across it stays the same. In a series circuit, one open switch would stop the current everywhere, but that is not how sockets are wired.
a.clue: Each appliance is on its own branch.

b.q: In Priya's home in Geelong, a lamp is on and a heater is then switched on in the same circuit. What happens to the total current in the supply wire?
opts: It rises, because the heater adds a branch current
It stays the same, because the voltage is unchanged
It falls, because the voltage is shared between them
It stays the same, because the lamp keeps its current
b.why: In parallel, the total current is the sum of the branch currents. The heater adds its own current to the lamp's, so the total rises. The voltage stays the same for each branch, but that does not mean the total current stays the same.

a.best: It keeps working with the same voltage across it

b.best: It rises, because the heater adds a branch current
